steps.title: Select your original in the game
steps.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own Super Mario 64 USA .z64 dump in the game’s ROM picker. The player verifies the original before loading it; the published Windows archive already contains the Godot player and its required companions.

presentation.manual_preparation: Choose Play, then select your own Super Mario 64 USA .z64 dump in the game’s ROM picker. The player verifies the original before loading it; the published Windows archive already contains the Godot player and its required companions. The game writes saves and backup saves through Godot user storage, normally AppData/Godot/app_userdata/Infinite Mario 64 on Windows. This is outside the package and outside Portcove backup. The transparency option can write project.godot beside the player; that exact configuration file is declared for compatible replacement and backup. The user-profile saves remain outside it. Keep a separate copy of that user folder; a customized data location can use external registration. Portcove replaces the managed runtime; existing external copies keep their files and update owner. Runtime rollback carries current declared data rather than rewinding saves; older-runtime and mod compatibility is not guaranteed.
